summary: SSO session affinity cookie mis-scope causes intermittent logout and blocked access to Support Insights analytics
summary_details: After yesterday's edge-proxy rollout, a subset of internal users are being logged out of Support Insights or see permission denied errors when switching teams. Issue reproduces primarily in Chrome and Electron-based console with long-lived sessions. Workaround (clearing cookies / incognito) temporarily restores access.
description:
Issue summary: Multiple internal users reported being unexpectedly signed out of the Support Insights analytics tool or receiving 403 on navigation after successful SSO. Impact: Internal engineers and SREs cannot view support analytics dashboards, blocking oncall investigations and escalation. Scope: ~8-12% of support staff across us-east region; replicated in staging with specific proxy config. Hypothesis: edge-proxy session affinity cookie was accidentally scoped to .redwood.ai instead of the internal top-level host during a canary config change, causing affinity to attach to the wrong backend pool and session lookup to fail when requests hit different path prefixes.

Environment details: Production | us-east cluster; Okta as IdP; auth-proxy version v2.7.1 deployed 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC. Affected clients: Chrome 114+, Electron Console v1.9.x.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Sign into console and open Support Insights dashboard (auth via Okta SSO).
2) Leave session idle for ~15 minutes or perform a team-switch from the header,
3) Observe that the page either redirects to /login or fails with a 403 JSON response when fetching /api/metrics,
4) Clearing cookies for .redwood.ai or opening in incognito restores access until next affinity jump.
logs_excerpt: 2026-03-10T01:12:04Z auth-proxy[proxy-a] INFO request id=xyz user=apatel cookie=SSO_AFF=poolB; domain=.redwood.ai path=/
2026-03-10T01:12:04Z auth-proxy[proxy-b] WARN request id=xyz session-lookup miss for sso_session=abc123; returning 403
comments: 2026-03-10T02:00:12Z - Miguel Torres: Acknowledged. Reproduced on Chrome. Initial triage suggests cookie scope changed in proxy template. Rolling a small repro in staging now.
2026-03-10T02:15:43Z - Aisha Patel: Affected users include oncall rotation for support and SRE. Need temporary mitigation so dashboards are available for alerts triage.

2026-03-11T09:04:01Z - SRE Team (channel #support): Canary rollback deployed to pool-a; monitoring for recurrence. Observed partial improvement but still seeing mixed-affinity headers on some clients.
investigation_notes: Checked proxy config diff: change set 0a1b2c3 updated cookie domain from internal.redwood.ai to .redwood.ai in template used for canary - likely intended to expand across subdomains but collided with internal host routing logic.

Cookie name SSO_AFF was previously host-scoped. Global domain allows browsers to send the cookie to both public and internal hostnames, causing mismatched backend selection in environment with path-based routing.
Session lookup service returns miss when requests cross from poolA to poolB because session KV is local to pool; fallback not implemented for cross-pool lookup.
Reproduction in staging by forcing cookie domain to .redwood.ai reproduces 403 within 2-3 team-switch attempts.
temporary_workarounds: Clear cookies for .redwood.ai in affected browsers
Use Incognito/Private mode to bypass persistent SSO_AFF cookie
Use direct IP-based access to support-insights (internal routing) as emergency bypass for oncall
resolution_plan: Immediate: Roll back the canary proxy template and redeploy previous host-scoped cookie config to all edge-proxy pools (completed 2026-03-11 02:45 UTC).
Short-term: Update proxy templates to set cookie domain explicitly to the internal host for internal services and add sticky session fallback (target 2026-03-13).
Medium-term: Implement shared session-store (Redis cluster) for cross-pool session lookup to avoid cookie-scoped routing reliance (proposal opened).
Follow-up: Add synthetic test in CI that validates SSO session continuity across team switches and proxy pool failover. Add a step to the deploy playbook that validates cookie domain on canary.
final_resolution_notes: 2026-03-11 02:45 UTC - Rollback completed; incident impact reduced to <1% and no new reports after rollback.
2026-03-12 16:00 UTC - Short-term proxy template change applied to all pools; QA passed in staging. Tracking medium-term work as RFC-134 on the infra backlog.
Owners: Miguel Torres (rollback & short-term changes), Priya Nair (session-store RFC), SRE oncall for monitoring
